provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1862 sets no commas around quaesumus in tribue quaesumus nobis; the typica prints cuius and the 1862 cujus; under the calendar's declared j orthography both project as cujus, so this is not a difference in the projected text. Corroboration: 1604 at line 38285, read as far as laudabiliter serviatur: tribue quae-; Venice 1570 at lines 52746-52752 reverses the order to tribue nobis, quesumus, which is a 1570 reading and not the 1862's.

propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Omnipotens et misericors Deus, de cujus munere venit, ut tibi a fidelibus
tuis digne et laudabiliter serviatur: tribue, quaesumus, nobis; ut ad
promissiones tuas sine offensione curramus. Per Dominum.

propers.name: Offertory
propers.text:
Precatus est Moyses in conspectu Domini Dei sui, et dixit: Quare, Domine,
irasceris in populo tuo? Parce irae animae tuae: memento Abraham, Isaac, et
Jacob, quibus jurasti dare terram fluentem lac et mel. Et placatus factus
est Dominus de malignitate, quam dixit facere populo suo.

propers.name: Secret
propers.text:
Hostias, quaesumus, Domine, propitius intende, quas sacris altaribus
exhibemus: ut, nobis indulgentiam largiendo, tuo nomini dent honorem. Per
Dominum nostrum.

propers.name: Postcommunion
propers.text:
Vivificet nos, quaesumus, Domine, hujus participatio sancta mysterii: et
pariter nobis expiationem tribuat, et munimen. Per Dominum.
